html:
Pataliputra was an ancient city on the Ganges in north India, on the site of today's Patna in Bihar. It began as a small fort and grew into the capital of the Maurya and Gupta empires.

Around 490 BCE King Ajatashatru of Magadha built a fort at the village of Pataligrama, where the Son river meets the Ganges, to fight the Licchavis across the river. His successor Udayin moved the capital there.

Under Chandragupta Maurya it became one of the largest cities in the world. The Greek envoy Megasthenes, in Megasthenes at Pataliputra, described a city about 15 km long with a timber wall, 570 towers and 64 gates.

  • Ashoka ruled from here, and a Buddhist council is said to have met here.
  • It was again the capital of the Guptas, and Aryabhata worked nearby at Kusumapura.

The city declined after the Gupta age and was in ruins when the Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang passed in the 7th century. Sher Shah Suri refounded it as Patna in the 16th century.
sum: Pataliputra was an ancient city on the Ganges in north India, on the site of today's Patna in Bihar. It began as a small fort and grew into the capital of the Maurya and Gupta empires.
